name: Airwallex
summary: A global financial platform combining online payment acceptance, multi-currency accounts, FX, transfers, cards, invoicing, and subscription billing.

pricing.headline: US domestic online cards are 2.8% + $0.30; international cards are 4.3% + $0.30, with regional rates elsewhere.
pricing.assumptions: Public US Explore-plan card pricing. International cards add 1.5%; subscription billing adds 0.5%; FX is 0.5% for major currencies and 1% for others. Local methods and regions vary.

sellerCoverage: Eligible businesses can open accounts in supported operating markets subject to entity, industry, and compliance checks.
buyerCoverage: Airwallex documents online acceptance across global card markets and more than 160 local payment methods, with multi-currency settlement.
products: Online commerce, SaaS, marketplaces, platforms, professional services, and global businesses needing payments plus treasury tools.

features.checkout: Hosted pages, payment links, components, APIs, SDKs, plugins, and mobile integrations.
features.subscriptions: Simple and hybrid subscriptions plus usage-based billing, invoicing, trials, and dunning.
features.invoicing: Global one-off and recurring invoices with reminders, credit notes, and reconciliation.
features.paymentMethods: Cards, wallets, BNPL, bank methods, and more than 160 local methods by market.
features.payouts: Like-for-like settlement into Airwallex wallets and transfers to supported bank destinations.

responsibilities.note: The business remains seller when using Airwallex Payments.

responsibilities.area: Sales tax, VAT, and product compliance
responsibilities.note: Payment and billing tools do not transfer tax registration or remittance responsibility.
Airwallex supplies risk and 3DS tools while the merchant owns configuration, evidence, and commercial exposure.
The platform supplies tools while the merchant configures pricing, currencies, and reconciliation.

strengths: Payments and multi-currency treasury in one platform
Public regional pricing in key markets
Strong cross-border settlement and FX tooling
limitations: Rates vary significantly by country and method
The merchant retains tax and compliance operations
avoidIf: You need a Merchant of Record
Your entity or primary market is unsupported
